task_description: Write a method in Dafny to check whether the given string starts and ends with the same character or not.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method StartsAndEndsWithSameChar(s: string) returns (result: bool)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The result is true if and only if the input string is non-empty and the first and last characters of the string are the same
- If the result is false, then either the string is empty or the first and last characters are different
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method StartsAndEndsWithSameChar(s: string) returns (result: bool)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - There are no preconditions, the method will always work. Strings are always not null.
    
Dafny specification:
    requires s != null
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result is true if the input string is non-empty and the first and last characters are the same
- The result is false if the string is empty or the first and last characters differ

Dafny specification:
    ensures result <==> (|s| > 0 && s[0] == s[|s| - 1])
  
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method StartsAndEndsWithSameChar(s: string) returns (result: bool)
  requires s != null
  ensures result <==> (|s| > 0 && s[0] == s[|s| - 1])
{
    if |s| == 0 {
        result := false;
    } else {
        result := s[0] == s[|s| - 1];
    }
}
```
